title: Maximum magnetic flux
description: Essential: The student must correctly calculate the maximum magnetic flux as Φ_m = B * A * N, where A is the coil area, yielding 0.048 Wb.

title: Maximum induced EMF
description: Essential: The student must correctly calculate the maximum induced EMF as E_m = N * B * A * ω, yielding 480π V.

title: Instantaneous EMF expression
description: Important: The student must provide the correct time-dependent expression e = E_m cos(ωt), with the correct numerical values substituted.

title: Average EMF for 30° rotation
description: Essential: The student must correctly apply Faraday's law for the average EMF over the given angular displacement, yielding 1440 V.

title: Area and unit conversion
description: Important: The student must correctly compute the coil area from the given side lengths, converting cm to m.

title: Application of Faraday's law
description: Important: The student must recognize that the instantaneous EMF is the negative time derivative of flux, leading to the sinusoidal form.

title: Cosine vs sine function
description: Pitfall: The student incorrectly uses a sine function for the instantaneous EMF, not matching the initial condition from the diagram.

title: Flux change calculation for average
description: Important: The student must correctly calculate the change in magnetic flux for the 30° rotation, using the initial and final angles.

title: Angular velocity in time calculation
description: Pitfall: The student incorrectly calculates the time interval for the 30° rotation, leading to a wrong average EMF.

title: Unit consistency and presentation
description: Optional: The student's final answers include correct SI units (Wb, V) and the expression is clearly presented.
